work_items.title: Native Rust workspace and reproducible builds
work_items.how: Pinned Rust 1.100.0 and locked Cargo graphs. The native runtime uses only the standard library, and its library/binary forbid unsafe code. Development and fuzz dependencies are separate from runtime code.
work_items.verification: Linux debug/release builds and Clippy passed locally and in PR #7.
work_items.limitations: This qualifies the lab toolchain only; crypto, storage and other runtime libraries remain undecided.

work_items.title: Bounded BER / LDAP decoder
work_items.how: Implemented checked definite BER lengths and integer/tag validation without recursion. Frames are capped at 16 KiB, with attribute count/name and DN bounds applied before accepting requests.
work_items.verification: Negative tests cover truncation, malformed lengths/IDs/tags, unsupported controls and attribute limits; generated inputs exercise bounded behavior.
work_items.limitations: Only the declared LDAP subset is decoded; this is not full LDAP or AD conformance.

work_items.title: Read-only RootDSE queries
work_items.how: Implemented empty-DN base searches for objectClass presence. Explicit attribute projection, *, +, 1.1 and typesOnly select static public metadata. No AD capability OIDs or naming contexts are advertised.
work_items.verification: The independent ldap3 client reads supportedLDAPVersion and vendor metadata from the running binary.
work_items.limitations: There are no users, groups, schema, directory state or general searches.

work_items.title: Credential rejection and safe diagnostics
work_items.how: Only anonymous access to public lab metadata succeeds. Credential/SASL binds fail. Parsed request/debug state retains no bind DN or password, and service diagnostics use static messages.
work_items.verification: Tests verify credential rejection, no credential echo in debug/response/stdout/stderr, and unsupported search failures.
work_items.limitations: This is a safeguard, not authentication or password management. There is no TLS; never send real credentials.

work_items.title: TCP framing and session budgets
work_items.how: Implemented fragmented/coalesced frame reads and a loopback-only, single-active-connection listener. Every read/write uses the remaining five-second total deadline; sessions stop after 32 requests.
work_items.verification: Socket tests cover idle deadlines, framing, public-interface refusal and request limits. A malformed peer does not kill the process.
work_items.limitations: The sequential listener is a lab design, not a production availability or throughput claim.

work_items.title: Independent client and packaged-binary checks
work_items.how: A separate Python ldap3 client launches the Rust process on an ephemeral loopback port. CI tests the release binary, then extracts the internal archive and tests that executable again.
work_items.verification: Positive RootDSE, credential denial, scope denial, malformed-peer recovery and extracted-binary checks passed.
work_items.limitations: This is Linux client evidence, not Windows domain join or a deployment qualification.

work_items.title: Property tests and core coverage gate
work_items.how: Added native negative/integration/property tests and instrumented coverage. The actual process is exercised in addition to direct parser tests; the core gate requires at least 90% lines.
work_items.verification: 21 Rust integration/property tests passed. Local measured core line coverage exceeded 90%; Python tooling had 34 passing tests and 98% combined coverage.
work_items.limitations: Core line coverage excludes test/CLI dispatch files. Percentages do not measure coverage of future AD functionality.

work_items.verification: 20,000 local address-sanitizer fuzz runs completed without a crash and without changing the lockfiles. Hosted PR #7 fuzz also passed.

problems.title: Caught SQL errors can make raw COMMIT completion look like a committed mutation
problems.detail: A real tokio-postgres 0.7.18/PostgreSQL 18.7 comparison shows that after a caught statement error, Transaction.commit() can return Ok while PostgreSQL rolls back the transaction and no inserted record exists. Raw SQL command completion alone is therefore not a durable mutation acknowledgment.
problems.resolution: The qualification helper tracks statement failures, rolls back and returns Aborted instead of successful commit. Deferred commit failures and lost connections never return success; unconfirmed commit outcomes conservatively discard the session and return UnknownCommit without automatic retry. Actual tests verify committed/absent database state.
problems.next_action: Carry this invariant into a typed authorized native adapter and constrain unmanaged transaction SQL. Qualify durable idempotency, caller-dropped-future safety and exact after-commit response loss; this helper does not close the wider I05/I26 production gaps.
problems.provenance: Observed with the real pinned database and Rust driver, then protected by executable helper regressions. This is a development correctness finding, not a GitHub setup incident or an upstream vulnerability claim.

problems.resolution: Added the bounded CRL profile with explicit expiration enforcement and unknown-status denial, replacement/retained-config semantics, RFC 9266 session binding and provider-fault tests. Independent probes and sanitizer/coverage gates now exercise the selected profile; missing boundary methods or skipped probes fail.
problems.next_action: Owner validation of the full Phase 0 packet; preserve the declared profile limits and separately qualify actual native product integration.
problems.provenance: Concrete native qualification gap and upstream default found by inspecting the selected library APIs and running owned synthetic handshakes; resolved for the stated engineering profile only.

problems.title: General revocation freshness and protected product TLS-key ingestion remain unqualified
problems.detail: Selected WebPKI checks CRL nextUpdate but not thisUpdate. The qualified owned-current-fixture profile does not establish external CRL freshness, maximum age, rollback protection, OCSP or intermediate-chain policy. Lab key permission checks also do not establish production owner/ancestor-race safety, zeroization, encrypted custody or HSM/provider recovery.
problems.next_action: Design and qualify trusted revocation acquisition/time/rollback policy and protected key provisioning before general CRL ingestion or valuable product credentials. Keep P01-14/P01-16 and integrated SEC-04/SEC-06 gates open; never promote the lab exporter to LDAP/EPA conformance.
problems.provenance: Actual selected-upstream revocation/time behavior and deliberately bounded native key-loader surface inspected during Phase 0 qualification; an explicit development integration risk, not a GitHub setup issue.

problems.title: Report refreshes duplicated CI events and Pages retries could overlook retained artifacts
problems.detail: The report refreshed for CI requested, in progress and completed events, with canceled pending runs in the Actions history. An unmerged closure or draft status change could leave stale PR metadata. A manual Pages retry stopped if the first successful CI run had a missing or expired artifact.
problems.resolution: Drop the requested trigger, refresh on unmerged closures and draft status changes, and search recent runs for an available dashboard artifact on the exact current main revision during manual Pages retries.
problems.next_action: Verify the report and Pages job summaries after the workflow lands on main.
